elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 13 retains automatic renewal ("This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods") and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied (no 60-day Vendor reminder; cap is 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%), so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods" — each renewal term is one year (12 months); existing language, unchanged.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year" — Client may opt out on 30 days' notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 13 nor the inserted sentence imposes any pre-renewal reminder obligation on TrueLink; the comment expressly declines to press it. To cure, add an operative obligation requiring TrueLink to notify Client at least 60 days before each renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence caps increases at "five percent (5%) in any renewal term", not the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13: notice of intent not to renew "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year" — a 30-day window, within the ≤60-day fallback. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a parser miss; the operative text states the 30-day figure in words and numerals.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term."

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the retained 30-day non-renewal window satisfies the ≤60-day element, and the single inserted sentence supplies the missing 5% renewal-pricing cap that Section 6's one-year freeze left open.

Preferred level fails on two elements: no Vendor reminder obligation at least 60 days before renewal, and the cap is 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%. The drafter would need an express reminder covenant and a lesser-of-CPI-and-3% formula to reach preferred.

Minimality holds: the redline adds one concise sentence and deletes nothing. The Section 6 one-year cost freeze and the most-favoured-rate covenant are retained, and no survival tails, procedures, notice mechanics or other extras outside the fallback checklist were added.

Intent preserved: the new cap operates only 'in any renewal term', so it does not contradict the Section 6 freeze covering the first year from the Effective Date, and the Section 12 termination cross-reference, dispute/documentation mechanics and discontinuation timelines in Section 13 are untouched. No undefined terms or dangling references are introduced.

Minor note for the rationale rather than a defect: the inserted cap refers to "TrueLink's fees" generally rather than Hosting Services fees specifically; this is broader in Client's favour and does not conflict with retained language.
